The child `exec`s an **interactive bash shell** (`bash -i`), while the parent holds the master fd to send keystrokes.\n\n### How each requirement is met\n\n| Requirement | Implementation |\n|---|---|\n| **Mimics a terminal** with interactive bash | `pty.fork()` + `os.execvpe(\"/bin/bash\", [\"bash\", \"-i\"], env)` — a real PTY makes bash run in interactive mode; commands are sent as characters + `\\n` |\n| **Supports interactive programs** | Because the child is on a real PTY, `isatty()` returns `True`, so vim, python REPL, `less`, `top`, etc. all work correctly |\n| **Modifier/control keys** | Keystrokes are written verbatim to the PTY master. The kernel's terminal line discipline interprets them: `\\x03`→SIGINT (Ctrl-C), `\\x1a`→SIGTSTP (Ctrl-Z), `\\x04`→EOF (Ctrl-D), `\\x1c`→SIGQUIT, etc. |\n| **Sources `~/.bashrc`** | `bash -i` (interactive, non-login) sources `~/.bashrc` by default — verified that `NVM_DIR` from `.bashrc` is present |\n\n### Key design details\n\n- **Background drain thread** continuously reads child output into an internal buffer, preventing kernel PTY buffer deadlocks when commands produce large output (tested with `seq 1 50000` — no hang).\n- **Non-blocking master fd** with retry logic on `EAGAIN`, so `send_keystrokes` never deadlocks even when the child isn't reading.\n- **`wait_sec`** causes a sleep after sending, giving commands time to execute.\n- **UTF-8 encoding** of keystrokes with `errors=\"replace\"` for safety.\n- **Clean lifecycle**: `close()` sends SIGHUP to the child's process group, joins the drain thread, closes the master fd, and reaps the child (with SIGKILL fallback). The child `exec`s an **interactive bash shell** (`bash -i`), while the parent holds the master fd to send keystrokes.\n\n### How each requirement is met\n\n| Requirement | Implementation |\n|---|---|\n| **Mimics a terminal** with interactive bash | `pty.fork()` + `os.execvpe(\"/bin/bash\", [\"bash\", \"-i\"], env)` — a real PTY makes bash run in interactive mode; commands are sent as characters + `\\n` |\n| **Supports interactive programs** | Because the child is on a real PTY, `isatty()` returns `True`, so vim, python REPL, `less`, `top`, etc. all work correctly |\n| **Modifier/control keys** | Keystrokes are written verbatim to the PTY master. The kernel's terminal line discipline interprets them: `\\x03`→SIGINT (Ctrl-C), `\\x1a`→SIGTSTP (Ctrl-Z), `\\x04`→EOF (Ctrl-D), `\\x1c`→SIGQUIT, etc. |\n| **Sources `~/.bashrc`** | `bash -i` (interactive, non-login) sources `~/.bashrc` by default — verified that `NVM_DIR` from `.bashrc` is present |\n\n### Key design details\n\n- **Background drain thread** continuously reads child output into an internal buffer, preventing kernel PTY buffer deadlocks when commands produce large output (tested with `seq 1 50000` — no hang).\n- **Non-blocking master fd** with retry logic on `EAGAIN`, so `send_keystrokes` never deadlocks even when the child isn't reading.\n- **`wait_sec`** causes a sleep after sending, giving commands time to execute.\n- **UTF-8 encoding** of keystrokes with `errors=\"replace\"` for safety.\n- **Clean lifecycle**: `close()` sends SIGHUP to the child's process group, joins the drain thread, closes the master fd, and reaps the child (with SIGKILL fallback). Supports context-manager (`with`) usage and `__del__` cleanup — no zombie processes.\n\n### No external dependencies\n\nThe implementation uses only Python standard library modules (`pty`, `os`, `select`, `termios`, `fcntl`, `struct`, `signal`, `threading`, `time`, `errno`), so nothing needed to be installed.\n\n### Bonus helper methods (beyond the interface)\n- `read_output(clear, timeout)` — retrieve accumulated child output\n- `is_alive()` — check if the shell is still running\n- `resize(rows, cols)` — resize the terminal window\n- `close()` / context manager — proper cleanup\n\n### Tests passed (15 total)\nBasic command execution, `.bashrc` sourcing, interactive shell detection, `isatty()` verification, Ctrl-C interrupt, Ctrl-Z suspend + `fg`, interactive Python REPL, Ctrl-D exit, context manager cleanup, large output without deadlock, real file"}}

This forks a child process and connects it to a fresh PTY as its controlling terminal. The child `exec`s an **interactive bash shell** (`bash -i`), while the parent holds the master fd to send keystrokes.\n\n### How each requirement is met\n\n| Requirement | Implementation |\n|---|---|\n| **Mimics a terminal** with interactive bash | `pty.fork()` + `os.execvpe(\"/bin/bash\", [\"bash\", \"-i\"], env)` — a real PTY makes bash run in interactive mode; commands are sent as characters + `\\n` |\n| **Supports interactive programs** | Because the child is on a real PTY, `isatty()` returns `True`, so vim, python REPL, `less`, `top`, etc. all work correctly |\n| **Modifier/control keys** | Keystrokes are written verbatim to the PTY master.
